reader.notes: The catalog row is Variadic 2..unbounded, so argument-1 alone is refused (COBOL1504 'at least 2; 1 given'), and ALL is admitted because the format repeats argument-2. The ALL expansion after a leading argument-1 evaluates with the right term count and exponents.

refuter.evidence: pvall.cob at --std 85: COMPUTE WS-N = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (WS-E (ALL)) with WS-E = 0 10 20 30 compiles and prints PV-ALL-ONLY 60.0000: the ALL table supplies argument-1 (0) AND the argument-2 series. IntrinsicBinder.cs#TryBindAllArgument admits ALL on sig.RepeatsAnArgument (MaxArgs == int.MaxValue), a property of the FUNCTION, not of the argument POSITION, and consults no edition. The reader's own requirement says 'argument-2 may be a table with ALL subscripts', which this acceptance exceeds. The 1985 text: §1989:A.2.2 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced ... ALL' and 'the effect is as if each table element ... were specified' (cite.py OK both). Reading A (the compiler's): the condition is on the function's definition and the as-if expansion PV(E(1) E(2) E(3) E(4)) fits the format, so it is legal. Reading B: the table reference stands for the repeated argument (argument-2) only, so a lone ALL reference leaves argument-1 unwritten and the form is outside §1989:A.2.34.2 'FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE ( argument-1 { argument-2 } … )' (cite.py OK) and must be refused. The text does not decide between them. Every other probe agrees with the format: Shared probes at --std 85 (run_probe.py, runs under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-177/runs): names.cob (data items named SQRT, RANGE, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, STANDARD-DEVIATION, legal user words at 85, used as arguments of their own functions) printed SQRT-NAME 4, RANGE-NAME 8, ORDMIN-NAME 2, PV-NAME 21, SD-NAME 0, all right; pvall.cob: SUM(WS-Q(ALL 2))=4, ORD-MIN(WS-Q(RX + 1 ALL))=2, RANGE(WS-Q(WS-I + 2 ALL))=1 (relative subscripts beside ALL), ORD-MIN(WS-S(ALL) "ABC")=2, ORD-MIN over group occurrences WS-R(ALL)=1, SD(WS-E(ALL) WS-E(ALL))=11.1803, PV(0 WS-Q(ALL ALL) 100)=113, all right; x_1.cob: IF FUNCTION SUM(1 2) = 3 AND FUNCTION ORD-MIN(WS-S(ALL)) = 2 -> IF-OK, ORD-MIN(WS-S(1)(2:2) "AAZ" "AB")=2, ORD-MIN(WS-S(ALL)(3:1))=2; refusals (one statement per file, --compile-only): r2_1 SUM(WS-A(ALL)) on a non-table COBOL2096; r2_2/r2_3 SUM(1 2)(1:1), ORD-MIN(3 1)(1:1) COBOL1629 (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR2); r2_4..r2_6 MOVE FUNCTION SQRT(4), DISPLAY FUNCTION RANGE(1 5), MOVE FUNCTION SUM(1 2) COBOL0900 (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4); x_2 ORD-MIN as a subscript COBOL0900; refuse2 SQRT(ALL)/SUM(ALL) COBOL0001; class c: c_1 N"..", c_2 X"..", c_3 1.0E2, c_4 WS-Q(WS-I * 2 ALL), c_5 B"1" each COBOL0900 at 85; c_7 ORD-MIN("B" ALL "A") accepted =2 (ALL literal is a 1985 figurative constant, length of the literal). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.2 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times'; OK §1989:A.2.2 'the effect is as if each table element associated with that subscript position were specified'; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR2; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4; OK §1985:VI.6.2.1 'the figurative constant ZERO (ZEROS, ZEROES)'; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 GRL2.3 'When the figurative constant ALL literal is not associated with another data item, the length of the string is the length of the literal'.
